title: Borealis AI Hosted vs Dedicated quickstart discovery
summary: Intro discovery to understand Borealis's time-to-first-token needs, whether Hosted or Dedicated is best fit, security constraints (data residency, KMS, SOC2), and to seed a pilot with free credits. Agreed to run a small hosted quickstart and measure latency/cost; SE to share benchmark checklist and security packet.
topics: hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs
pilot scope: 1 model, 2 endpoints, baseline SLA
action_items: Alex Mercer: send pricing sheet + quickstart instructions + credits redemption link (due 2026-05-24)
Maya Chen: share benchmark checklist (latency/cost telemetry) and small sample curl + python snippets (due 2026-05-23)
Jordan Patel: confirm list of 3 sample prompts and expected QPS for POC (due 2026-05-26)
next_steps: Run hosted quickstart with free credits; Redwood to provide credentials and example repo
Schedule POC kickoff next week once sample prompts are received
Security team to follow up with SOC2 docs and KMS integration notes
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-21T15:00 PT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Alex Mercer (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Jordan Patel (Borealis CTO), Priya Rao (ML Eng Lead), Samir Das (Platform Eng)
Links shared: Redwood quickstart repo (https://redwood.ai/quickstart - shared in chat), security packet (link), pricing spreadsheet (link)

[00:00] Alex (AE): hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. i'm alex from redwood inference, and with me is maya our solutions eng. how's everyone doing?
[00:10] Jordan (CTO): good, yeah thanks alex. uh we're excited to see how quickly we can get something up. we're heavy on latency needs, and we want to understand whether hosted or dedicate makes more sense.
[00:18] Maya (SE): great, thanks. quick agenda — do a 10-minute context / current stack, then talk hosting options and time-to-first-token, then agree pilot scope and next steps. sound good?
[00:28] Priya (ML): yeah that works. real quick background — we're building an in-product assistant for our analytics platform, aiming for sub 300ms median generation for short prompts, about 50 token answers. volume is small to start, maybe 5-20 qps per tenant. privacy is a big thing — EU data residency, and we want KMS integrations.
[00:45] Samir (Platform): also we use Okta SAML SSO and have strict audit log requirements. platform team will need RBAC and token lifecycle controls.
[00:55] Alex (AE): perfect. that helps a lot. can i ask about timeline and success criteria — when would you like to have a working pilot?
[01:05] Jordan: ideally 2-3 weeks. success is: 1) time-to-first-token under a day for devs, 2) a small pilot running on hosted, and 3) initial latency + cost numbers to inform whether we move to dedicated or private.
[01:18] Maya (SE): cool, that fits our PLG quickstart approach. hosted API gives fastest time-to-first-token — we can have credentials and an example repo working same day; free credits cover pilot tokens. dedicated gives you predictable throughput and can be stood up in a few weeks depending on capacity booking. private (VPC/on-prem) is longer and usually for regulatory customers.
[01:35] Priya: can you clarify what "predictable throughput" means — is that per-tenant GPU pools?
[01:40] Maya: yeah so dedicated is reserved GPU pools for your org, you get a capacity reservation and can configure autoscale policies. it's more expensive but you trade cost variance for throughput predictability.
[01:50] Jordan: latencies — if we compare hosted vs dedicated, could hosted achieve sub 300ms for our 50-token answers?
[01:56] Maya: it depends on model and region. our curated smaller models can hit that in hosted for short sequences with continuous batching tuned — but there is more tail variance on shared hosted. dedicated will reduce that tail and let you pin model versions and quantize aggressively. also caching — prefix and KV cache helps a lot on repeated prompts.
[02:15] Samir: i heard the term KV cash on a blog — is that the same as KV cache?
[02:19] Priya: yeah the transcriber messed it up.
[02:22] Alex (AE): ha, KV cache. good.
[02:24] Maya: another callout — we can ship suggestions for quantization profiles, which can reduce cost by 40-60% with minor quality impact for some workloads. we'll need sample eval prompts to recommend the right profile.
[02:37] Jordan: about security: do you have SOC 2 and ISO? and for keys we need KMS — can we use our AWS KMS?
[02:44] Alex: yes, we have SOC 2. private and dedicated can integrate with customer-managed KMS/HSM; hosted can integrate via customer KMS for key wrapping on request. we'll share the compliance pack.
[02:56] Priya: and VPC peering? some of our data must remain inside our VPC — is that supported for dedicated?
[03:03] Maya: Dedicated can be set up with a private peering and private control plane; private on-prem is required if you need air-gapped. We'll include network diagrams in the packet.
[03:14] Jordan: okay. what about SSO and RBAC? our security team will want SCIM and SAML and fine-grained roles.
[03:20] Alex: we support SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning, and role-level permissions — we'll attach our RBAC doc.
[03:27] Samir: about logging and audit — retention and export? we need to push audit logs to our SIEM.
[03:33] Maya: logs can stream to customer endpoints; we also provide per-route telemetry and token-level cost breakdowns in the console. export to S3 or push via forwarders to Splunk/Datadog is common.
[03:45] Jordan: great. on the quickstart — can you walk through the fastest path to first token?
[03:50] Maya: sure. Step 1: we create an org in hosted, issue API keys, and give you a sandbox project. Step 2: clone the quickstart repo and run the sample python script that hits our streaming endpoint. Step 3: run your sample prompts and capture latency metrics. We can provision credits that cover the pilot. Typically developers get first token in under an hour if they follow the repo.
[04:12] Priya: do you have code examples for our internal SDK? we use golang and node mostly.
[04:16] Maya: yes — we have node, python, and go snippets in the repo. i'll drop go examples in the checklist.
[04:23] Jordan: how are you measuring latency? -- median vs p95? we care about both.
[04:28] Maya: we'll instrument both median and p95; the benchmark checklist includes sequence-length distributions, cold start behavior, and side-by-side cost per 1K tokens for different models and quantizations.
[04:40] Jordan: competitors: we've looked at OpenAI and Anthropic; their hosted offerings are simple but costs vary. we like that you offer a migration path to dedicated and private.
[04:51] Alex (AE): that's a common pattern. Redwood's differentiator is the unified interface across hosted/dedicated/private and the ops controls to tune economics.
[04:59] Priya: about pricing — any rough numbers for a small dedicated cluster? (we expect ~20 qps peak across tenants)
[05:06] Alex: rough order: depends on GPU type and SLA, but our initial estimate for a small reserved pool that matches 20 qps on smaller LLMs would be in the low tens of thousands per month; we'll send a tailored quote after we see your sample prompts and expected token volumes.
[05:22] Jordan: ok. one more — compliance and data retention in EU. We need to ensure EU residency for logs and optionally model data.
[05:30] Maya: hosted has EU regions; for guaranteed residency we recommend dedicated in an EU region or private on-prem. we'll include region options in the packet.
[05:40] Samir: question on fallback: if dedicated loses capacity can you auto-failover to hosted to keep things alive?
[05:46] Maya: yes we support smart routing and fallback policies — you can route to compatible model variants in hosted as a fallback, with observability to know when fallbacks occur.
[05:55] Jordan: perfect. let's talk pilot scope — what would you recommend for a 2-week pilot?
[06:00] Maya: recommend: 1) hosted quickstart with 2 endpoints using one lightweight model and one slightly larger for comparison; 2) provide 10 sample prompts and 1K tokens total across tests; 3) measure median and p95 latency, cost per 1K tokens, and regression checks. We'll give a small credit allocation to cover it.
[06:20] Alex (AE): to summarize — Redwood will: share quickstart repo, provision credits, send benchmark checklist, and take sample prompts; Borealis will confirm prompts, run the hosted test, and share results.
[06:31] Jordan: yep, timeline: we'll try to run this week and get results by next Friday.
[06:36] Priya: i'll own prompt set and run the tests.
[06:39] Samir: i'll loop in security to review SOC2 packet and KMS notes.
[06:43] Alex (AE): great. any other blockers or questions?
[06:46] Jordan: none from me. a small nit — we may need to test multi-tenant isolation patterns; do you have examples?
[06:52] Maya: yes, we'll include a best-practice doc for multi-tenant tenancy, rate-limits per tenant, and per-tenant caching keys.
[06:59] Alex (AE): ok, action items — i'll email the pricing and credits link; maya will share the benchmark checklist and go snippets. jordan/priya will send prompts. security will follow with SOC2 requests.
[07:10] Jordan: thanks everyone.
[07:12] Alex (AE): thanks all. we'll follow up with the packet and a calendar invite for the POC kickoff.

End of transcript.
